source.title: Re-understanding Graph Unlearning through Memorization
source.authors: Peng-Fei Ding; Yan Wang; Guan-Feng Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, though some figure and table text is garbled or flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study ranks graph training nodes by a memorization score, removes nodes, retrains models, and reports the resulting test performance. This bears conceptually on V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports other unlearning comparisons, attack results, and parameter analyses, but they do not test the listed claim versions. Figure 4 provides the relevant test-performance comparisons; its plotted values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study uses memorization to develop graph-unlearning methods. Its removal experiment measures a related claim: nodes are ranked by a composite of absolute self-prediction change and effects on neighbors, rather than V8's signed effect of inclusion on predicting the example's own label. Removing nodes also removes their connected edges.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the Figure 4 discussion, provided 'memorization' means the graph-specific composite score. The paper's broader conclusion is that memorization informs unlearning difficulty and that MGU improves forgetting quality, efficiency, and utility preservation.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines graph neural networks on node-classification graphs and retrains after removing nodes ranked by a graph-specific memorization score; it does not use the original image-classification setup in V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization effect depends on which nodes are removed (hard-to-unlearn versus random or easy) and on the unlearning ratio; the text specifically notes little effect for random or easy removal at small ratios.

fits_no_version.finding: On Cora-GAT and Citeseer-GCN, retraining after removing high composite-memorization nodes substantially reduces test accuracy; equal random or low-score removal has little effect at small removal ratios.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing nodes ranked highly by a graph-specific score combining self-prediction changes and neighbor effects harms GNN test accuracy more than equal random removal at small removal ratios.

record.problems: The relevant test-performance results are plotted without precise values in the supplied text. The text describes substantial degradation and little effect at small ratios but provides no uncertainty for Figure 4.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly test the listed versions. Other unlearning-method comparisons and attack evaluations concern graph-unlearning quality or the paper's proposed method.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

Removal ranked specifically by the signed effect of inclusion on the example's own correct-label prediction, compared with equal random removal. No separate removal experiment using that score is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the changed selection construct, not merely the new datasets or architectures. Figure 4's precise curve values and uncertainty cannot be recovered from the supplied text; qualitative differences are explicitly stated.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Network width and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and the training-test gap.
The study uses graph node memorization and reports test performance after retraining; it does not test ResNet-50 or the stated CIFAR-100/ImageNet/MNIST settings.

rows.subject: Cora-GAT
rows.operation_detail: Retrained after removing the hard-to-unlearn nodes, ranked by memorization score.
rows.measure: Test accuracy after retraining, compared with the original model.
rows.note: The text says removing hard-to-unlearn nodes leads to substantial degradation; precise plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Substantial test-accuracy degradation is stated, but selection uses the composite graph score in Eq. (2), so this does not establish V8's effect.

rows.subject: Cora-GAT
rows.operation_detail: Retrained after removing randomly selected nodes.
rows.measure: Test accuracy after retraining, compared with the original model.
rows.note: The text says removing the same number of random nodes has little effect at small unlearning ratios.
rows.check: A valid random-removal control for the graph experiment, but not an independent test of V8. Little effect is stated only for small removal ratios; the row spans all plotted ratios.
